examples.name: Primary action
examples.description: The main action in a form, dialog, or workflow.

examples.name: Lower-emphasis destructive action
examples.description: An outlined destructive action for when it shouldn't be the loudest control in its group, e.g. beside a primary Save.

examples.name: Loading submit
examples.description: A loading form submit button that keeps its size and accessible name.

examples.name: Icon before
examples.description: A button with a leading icon.

examples.name: Icon after
examples.description: A button with a trailing icon.

examples.name: Full width
examples.description: A button that fills its container.

examples.name: Inverse (on a dark surface)
examples.description: The on-dark treatment for placement on a dark or bold-colored surface such as a Banner - transparent fill, inverse content, white subtle overlays on hover/press.

examples.name: Disabled (secondary prominence)
examples.description: A disabled button using native disabled behavior. prominence="secondary" (the default) keeps a visible border (color-border-disabled), matching its own resting bordered look.

examples.name: Disabled (primary/tertiary prominence)
examples.description: prominence="primary" and prominence="tertiary" stay borderless when disabled (border-color: transparent), matching their own resting borderless look - applying the same border color used on prominence="secondary" here would draw a border that was never part of the design.

antiExamples.name: Navigation
antiExamples.reason: Use LinkButton or Link for navigation-only behavior.

antiExamples.name: Toggle state
antiExamples.reason: Use ToggleButton for selected/unselected button state.
